findings.title: include_website_name missing question mark breaks AMS inclusion check
findings.body: The method is defined as `include_website_name` instead of `include_website_name?`. ActiveModel::Serializer's attribute inclusion mechanism relies on `include_<attr>?` methods; without the trailing `?`, this method will not be recognized as the inclusion predicate for `website_name` and the attribute's visibility logic (returning nil when website is blank) won't be honored consistently with the rest of the codebase's pattern (e.g. `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_user_fields?`). This could cause `website_name` to always be serialized (relying only on the method returning nil) or inconsistent behavior across serializer versions.

findings.title: website_name logic duplicated from removed JS computed property without shared tests for edge cases
findings.body: The three-branch domain comparison logic (exact match, same TLD+1 generic check requiring >2 segments, suffix check) is intricate and only exercised by 3 happy-path specs. Edge cases such as discourse_host having exactly 2 segments (e.g. 'example.com') combined with a website_host with more subdomains, or malformed URIs, are not covered, risking incorrect display or exceptions in production for malformed website values (though `rescue nil` guards URI parsing, but note it swallows all errors including unrelated ones).

findings.title: Leftover incorrect doc comment reference
findings.body: The doc comment for `profileBackground` was changed from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground`, but this diff is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (website path display) and is just incidental cleanup; not a functional issue, but indicates the `websiteName` computed property removal in user.js.es6 controller was not matched with equivalent removal/rename everywhere, e.g., model computed `profileBackground` naming confusion suggests leftover artifacts from a copy-paste of the old `websiteName` property.
